evals.name: unknown-over-any-on-untrusted-input
evals.prompt: I've got a webhook handler in src/webhook.ts that takes the raw parsed JSON body and pulls out an `eventName` string and a `retryCount` number. Right now the body param is typed `any` and it's leaking everywhere downstream. Can you rewrite it so it's actually type safe?
evals.expected_output: A handler whose input is typed `unknown` (not `any`), narrowed with an explicit type guard or assertion predicate before any property access, with an explicit return type, and an error path that throws or returns a typed Result rather than returning a partially-typed object.
assertions: Property access happens only after a type guard / `in` check / typeof narrowing
The exported function has an explicit return type annotation
No `as any` or unexplained `as` assertion is introduced

evals.name: discriminated-union-over-optional-props
evals.prompt: This is getting out of hand — our upload state is one interface with `isLoading?`, `data?`, `error?` and `progress?` all optional, and every consumer has to null-check four fields in combinations that can't actually happen. There are four real states: nothing started, uploading with a percentage, finished with a file URL, failed with an error. Can you model this properly in TypeScript?
evals.expected_output: A discriminated union with a shared literal discriminant (e.g. `status`), one member per real state carrying only the data valid for that state, plus a consumer that switches on the discriminant and closes with an exhaustive `never` check.
assertions: A discriminated union with a shared literal discriminant replaces the optional-property interface
Each member carries only the fields valid in that state (no optional data/error on every member)
A consumer switches on the discriminant
An exhaustiveness check via `never` (assertNever or `const _x: never = state`) is present

evals.name: strict-esm-node-project-setup
evals.prompt: Starting a small Node 20 library from scratch, publishing as ESM only. Need a tsconfig and the initial src layout. I want the compiler as strict as it'll reasonably go — I'd rather fight it now than debug undefined at 2am.
evals.expected_output: A tsconfig with `strict: true` (not individual flags), `module`/`moduleResolution` set to Node16 or NodeNext, `declaration: true` for a library, and the extra safety flags such as `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`; `"type": "module"` in package.json; and relative imports written with the `.js` extension in `.ts` source.
assertions: tsconfig sets `strict: true` rather than enabling individual strict flags
`declaration: true` is set (library consumed by other TypeScript)
At least one extra safety flag such as `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is suggested
Any relative import shown in .ts source carries the `.js` extension
